It's not an issue that he was asked about, and I don't even think that he was present in the region during this period of time. I'll have to double check that but -- but this Operation Neretva, et cetera, the witness's testified that he had a fairly discrete set of responsibilities and task that he conducted. It seems to me that questions about these issues are going to go well beyond the scope of the direct examination and also well beyond really what the witness's own area of responsibility was, his competence, and his knowledge, based on the things that he was doing in the region. So it doesn't seem to be a very helpful at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Praljak, if I've understood you well, the Defence, by using the documents and putting questions to the witness address the Neretva operation in 1993. Is that what you're getting at? Perhaps the way you are proceeding is not ideal. We have spent a lot of time looking at the document already. You should have put the question to the witness and ask him, "Do you know this document? Have you seen it before? As this is a document which is dated September, perhaps he's seen the document, perhaps he hasn't seen the document. He arrived, as it seems, at a latter stage. So you should ask him when he arrived, and when he arrived was he shown documents that had been drafted before he arrived? He would have said yes, or no. And after that, you should have discussed the document and the references in the document, to discover whether, in September, there was an offensive that had been launched by the ABiH. He would have said yes or no. He might have known, he might not have known. As he was in charge of logistics, if he doesn't know, then you move on to something else. So, pick it up along those lines, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I've been listening to the witness very carefully because I'm a very good listener. He told us earlier this morning that he inspected all the documents when he arrived on the 23rd. This happened on the 19th, very shortly before that. We are talking about continuity here. Second of all, the witness stated clearly that he was not a logistics man, he was a member of the combat group that provided the logistics of the UNHCR. He was not making a list of tins and ammunition, if I heard the witness well, and if I understood him well. Since at the time the convoys passed through the combat sector of an offensive that we have already spoken about, my approach, I don't know how else to call it, but I can ask him whether he's familiar with the document. But it says in the document what was going on there, that there was an attack ongoing. I really --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you answer that question, please, Witness, now? In light of this document, you arrived on the 23rd, a few days after which this document was drafted. Did you know, as you assumed your duties that there had been an offensive launched by the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, maybe I should just say something that General Praljak may not have seen. In the distribution list, it seems that the witness has been provided with this document. The witness should have a look at the document instead of us closing the session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try and make the whole story shorter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: From the documents, witness, that you have received and that you can find in the Prosecutor's binder, a reference is made to a number of things starting with the existence of operation, and I'm going to skip those that preceded your arrival, the attack on Hum, the attack on Mostar on the 28th and the 21st of September. To which extent were you aware or did you feel the combat activities in that area and according to your information was it the BiH army that attacked or rather the HVO? I'm talking about Vrdi, Hum, Mostar, Buna. I'm talking about these attacks. You went there once a week. Did you know anything about these things at the time? I believe that my question was really simple.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, I think just for the record, we should probably have a redaction of that bit of testimony. Because it could tend to identify the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Registrar, please could you -- could we have an order? Please proceed, Mr. Praljak.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: My question again is very simple. I am just going to deal with two problems. Can the witness please be shown these two maps? Did you know irrespective of who the addressee of the document is, did you see, did you feel, were you aware of the fact that the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina at that time and prior to your arrival but in any case during your stay there, carried out offensive against the HVO in the entire south sector of its theatre of war from Dreznica to Vrdi towards Siroki Brijeg towards Mostar, Hum and Buna? Just tell me briefly. I am familiar, I am not familiar. I saw, I didn't see.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW
utterances.text: Yes. I was going to answer before, but I was just telling you about that exception. I have said before that we didn't have as a task the control of military operations, and therefore I didn't follow that up. You know very well that in a military organisation, there is a norm which is need-to-know, and therefore, only the information is only addressed to who has to get that information. I don't know whether what were the military operations of the HVO and the BiH. Now, the changes of command or a front in the Dreznica area, well, I always had the same type of controls coming from the HVO and the BiH controls.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry for intervening, Witness. We have a document, there is no doubt that this document speaks of an offensive. These -- this is information gathered by SpaBat. We also note that the HVO is concentrating troops in Gradina. The hypothesis is that the HVO is preparing a counteroffensive. This military situation is very precise and this is something worth mentioning. 72 HVO soldiers have been captured in Vrdi. Therefore, we are dealing with an obvious military situation. You are charged, as you said, with the security of humanitarian convoys. For a simple mind, it is easy to think that there is a military operation underway. This may have an impact on humanitarian convoys, on their movements. So -- which is apparently under your responsibility. So when you arrived four days after this document was drafted, were there any briefings with your commanding colonel? Did you assess the situation and, at SpaBat level, which were the consequences of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can't really tell you more than what this document says. I say that I might know about this document because during our preparation and possibly during those days I was travelling by boat towards Split where I got to on the 23rd, but possibly we knew about this topic. But what I want to say is that if I can't provide you with more information right now, it's because I was not really involved in the analysis of the situations. You are obviously right if a counteroffensive is being prepared or any type of combat, this obviously affected the security of convoys, but what happened then is that convoys didn't leave the place, either the parts didn't offer their agreement, or I didn't get the order to escort any of the convoys. And this happened many times. Many times we weren't able to send convoys to the area of Jablanica because we were told that there were conflicts in Vrdi many, many times when I was there. So what I have told General Praljak is that always, with some -- with maybe some geographic changes in the front, I have always had to go through the HVO lines and the BiH lines, and practically always at the same place. That is why I can't provide you with more information than what you can here see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. General Praljak, the witness has answered. Do you really want to insist or can you move on to another topic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to move on to a different topic. I would just like to read out paragraph 10 of the witness's statement which says, "Before going to Bosnia we got the documents of the Main Staff, like reports, as well as documents from the General Staff. We were from the previous task force, Canarias. We were lectured by those who had been in Bosnia as to the general situation and as to military procedures." On the basis of this paragraph of the statement, I started my cross-examination, convinced that the witness will be able to testify about basic things.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Sir, you're a professional soldier. I would like to move on to a different topic before I move on to mortars, yet another topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, now, look, it's five past 4.00. We need to have a break before you move on to your next topic. You'll deal with that later. You know, time flies. I've just noticed what time it was. We are going to have a 20 minute break and unfortunately, remember, we have to finish by 5.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have another 40 minutes before the end of the hearing.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Witness, before I move on to another area, just one more document. It is a Prosecution document that I would like us to look at, P06452, 6452. It's a document from SpaBat dated the 5th of November 1993. While you're looking for it, I am going to read the portion referring to East Mostar which is on page 3 of the Croatian version, East Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, could we get the number again of that exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. P06452, P06452. It's your own document, I mean a Prosecution document, the date is the 5th of November 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The witness -- it's in the binder that doesn't -- it's in the documents to your right. Yes, sir. It's not in a binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, this document is in which binder? Because we have to find it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Binder 3D, 6452. P, P, P06452.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Kovacic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't know which Prosecution binder it is in because we do not receive the same binder as the Trial Chamber does. We are just given the raw documents and then we put them together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This document is in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, because our case managers do their best to put them into binder form to speed up the process but otherwise...

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's in my documents, P06452.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Have you found it, sir? Let's take a look at East Mostar and what it says there. According to the observer reports from the United Nations, on the 3rd of November, the Serbs fired six tank shots on HVO positions and mortars in the Blagaj area. And now the comment, "This confirms Serb operations as support to the BH army, it seems that the Serbs are continuing to lend their support to the weaker side, depending on the region, so that the fighting can continue." End of comment. So on page 5 of the Croatian text, that's where you'll be able to find it, point 3, it says, "It is claimed that four truck loads of weapons have arrived in Mostar, coming from the Bosnian Serb army. It is also claimed that they bought two heavy mortars and have two tanks on loan with crews from the Bosnian Serbs, and they are opening fire on targets selected -- on selected targets -- targets selected by BiH." And my question to you is this: Did you know that the army of Republika Srpska, on a regular basis, both before and during the time you were there, bombed Mostar both the west bank and the east bank, especially during the night? Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW
utterances.text: No. I had no knowledge about Serb shelling of West Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, your remit was to take humanitarian convoys and you usually parked them in Marshal Tito street when you came to Mostar. Is that right, that you would be in Marshal Tito street mostly during the night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Sir, between the right and left side, you have high buildings. Now from any HVO position, could you see position -- the position where you stopped with your APCs? You were there. Could you see any HVO positions from the buildings or, rather, from HVO positions, could you see where -- the place where you had stopped with your APCs in Marshal Tito street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW
utterances.text: From where the vehicles were parked, it was difficult to see anything of West Mostar because we have the house in between or right in front of our eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you. During the night, according to your reports, and what was known, your men were in the APCs; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW
utterances.text: Yes, true.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: And from the APCs, they heard some explosions. Tell us, sir, with what degree of certainty can a soldier in an APC conclude, A, where the projectiles are falling, and where the projectiles are coming from, at night, in Marshal Tito street, in a closed APC, counting some shells coming from somewhere and falling somewhere? What would the certainty be of soldiers knowing where these projectiles were coming from and where the shells were falling?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW
utterances.text: Well, I'd say to a high degree. Not everyone was aboard the vehicles. There was security patrolling outside the vehicles. And as to know where the shots were being fired from, which is what you're asking about, we undertook a number of tests via the sappers through the study of the grenade handles, and from the studies we concluded that the grenades came from West Mostar. There was an explosion in West Mostar ascribed by the HVO to the other side. I remember that studies were undertaken and it resulted -- basically was concluded it was a charge, what was being talked about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Witness, please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the last sentence? It seems that it was not quite understood. It's not fully transcribed what was the matter with this grenade, this explosion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The study of the handle is a way of identifying the direction from which the grenade came from. We undertook such studies both in West Mostar and once in East Mostar, in order to know whether the grenade came from the Serb side, and on that occasion, as it happened, it was a precharged grenade, charged in situ.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, let us try to clarify this. SpaBat counted the number of shots, of explosions, at night-time. We saw indeed a chart compiling on a daily basis the number of shots or shells. Very well. During the night, your soldier will be observing. If there is an outgoing shot, can you, in the middle of the night, determine where it comes from, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, unless you see the flash light of the shot. However, you can get some idea of where the sound is coming from, as from where the sound is coming from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Back at the time, did you know where the Serbian forces were positioned? Did you know what those positions were around Mostar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we see in this document an observation that comes from your own tactical group, the Madrid tactical group. It is said that "This information confirms Serbian actions in support of the ABiH in Mostar." Because it seems that the Serbs want to support the ABiH in order to keep the fighting going. This mention is important because it implies normally or it involves the Serbs in what is happening in Mostar. So based on this type of information, did your command request a finer analysis of the information or more information? Because this is not a neutral piece of information. In a conflict between two parties, the ABiH and the HVO, we see that there is a third party that plays a part. This is what is being said by the document. So, at your level, did you have a debriefing session, an assessment, steps to be undertaken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is information from the military observers, Your Honour, and I have no more information aside what is here in the report. Aside from what the comment says.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So, your rank is of-- is such that with information of this kind, well, you must be appraised of them. It would be unbelievable that number 2 or number 3 in SpaBat would have no knowledge whatsoever of this information which at least at the military if not the political level, has some consequences.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. More at the political level. I was not the second in command of the battalion. I explained the flow chart, or the command structure of the Madrid Task Force already. Perhaps we did talk about it, or perhaps I dealt with it because this is an INTREP of which I'm the recipient amongst others. What I'm trying to say to this courtroom is that I have no further comments. Perhaps there were consequences and other reports by our group, but I do not recall undertaking any specific mission to verify the veracity of this information. Generally speaking, information gathering operations with the different parties were undertaken by the battalion, and all that derived from such information gathering activities did not, in fact, impinge on the duties of my battalion. There was no reason for me to know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Witness, I'll repeat the question again. At [indiscernible] we have many years. Now, we are both soldiers. At night in Marshal Tito street, in an APC in town, are there any realistic possibilities for you, without any further investigation, angle of impact, can you with any degree of certainty confirm the report and ascribe this to the HVO? And say that the shells that fell in East Mostar came from HVO positions? As a soldier, can you say that at all?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I object to the question, Mr. President, because it's already been asked and it's already been answered by this witness who I believe testified in his view had a high degree of confidence. This very question was asked and answered already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Praljak, the question you asked him is a question that's been asked already. Perhaps you might want to address this question in a different way.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: On the technical aspect a very precise technical aspect, Marshal Tito street. That's what I asked him about. In a street that's not too wide, with buildings on either side, at night, people are in their high-rise buildings, you're a professional soldier, so with what degree of certainty can the shells falling all over the place be ascribed to the HVO? You can say "on the basis of the sound, the type of sound, I can say such and such."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW
utterances.text: General, it's been 14 years since events took place. Plenty of efforts went into our mission, our tour of duty there. Perhaps now technically I cannot prove anything because we would have to take a study of the field. As you know, you can drive along Marshal Tito street from the HVO territory and not just perpendicular to the street. I can assure you that the whole of my battalion felt and were persuaded that the shots arriving at East Mostar came from the HVO troops. I cannot exclude that some were of Serb origin. I have no data to prove or disprove that, but most of the shelling falling in Mostar is, you know, by all concerned considered to have been HVO shelling. Nobody had any doubts about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you. I am happy with your answer. We have talking about evidence. We are in court here. I'm going to ask you this, sir. According to the points that you established and we already saw in previous pieces of evidence, your part of the battalion, according to your choice, you were in the area of war activities. We are talking war here. Tell me, please, is it the right of every command, would the command of the 4th Corps be a legitimate military target, and is there a right in war to target that legitimate military target? That would be my first question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW
utterances.text: Allow me to say that it would be a military objective, full stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you. The command of the 1st -- 41st Brigade, was it also a military target?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: And what about every possible mortar position that you can find in that same part of Mostar? Would these also be legitimate military targets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW
utterances.text: Yes, that too is true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Praljak, these are all legal questions, questions of law, and the witness is here to ask questions on fact.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Judge Trechsel, I'm a bit short on time, and this is just a matter of the procedure. I have 15 documents in which it says literally 15 documents, Prosecutor's documents, in which it says the following: "We have again tried to prevent the positioning of the mortars of the BiH army near the hospital." I can give you a whole list of these documents. I've already done that. We have tried to prevent but we failed. We just tried. In the same documents, it says that the BiH army has a mortar on the tractor, it says that the BiH army has a mortar on a lorry. This is what is stated in these documents, the document number is P07408, East Mostar, the BiH army placed mortars all over the town, and they are being used at random. They placed mortars, they are firing shells, and then they are changing positions. The document is P07408. I'm talking in very simple terms here, what are military targets? This is not a legal question. This is just my question. This is a military question. Maybe somebody else can put the same question. I'm talking about legitimate military targets, the military, the communications, the weapons I've just asked a simple military question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Without addressing any legal questions, witness, let us assume because here we are talking about military assumptions, let's assume that the Spanish army is involved in a conflict and faces a situation where the enemy has its headquarters in a particular location, his -- its troop in another location. Do you think that in military terms you would be able to fire shots at the headquarters of the enemy, fire shots on a location which might be a hospital but which is surrounded by mortars? In military terms, what do you say to this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it's very difficult to give a concrete answer to such a difficult question. Armies are subject to international law and the rules of war. The shelling of populated centres is something which in principle should not take place. One would have to find procedures that would allow sufficient accuracy in order to avoid collateral damage. It is part of the responsibility of commanders to take one action or another, and then it's up to the Courts of law to judge what is right and what is wrong. It's not up to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Sir, you've answered my question. Mr. Praljak?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: P06568, P06568. This is a document in the Prosecutor's binder, P06568. Have you found the document, sir? Please look at the page 4 of the B/C/S text and towards the end of that page, a reference to the dam in Salakovac. On that same day on the 8th some information is received at the dam at Salakovac is in a difficult position because of the rain, no party has a free access and there is a major risk -- and now, is the witness receiving interpretation into Spanish?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Page 4 in B/C/S, a reference is made to the dam in Salakovac. Towards the end of the page it says this: "On the 8th, information has been received that the dam in Salakovac is in a bad situation, that no party has free access to the outlet valve, and there is a risk that the dam could collapse in which case the whole Neretva valley might be flooded. The engineers on both sides established contacts in order to negotiate and talk about the dam." My question is this: Are you familiar with the situation and are you aware of the fact that the BiH army closed the valves on the dam, they had the control at the time, and they threatened that they would release the water at a high pressure from the lake and that they would flood the entire valley of the Neretva River? Are you familiar with that? Can you tell us something about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW
utterances.text: I recall this issue of the dam, yes, there was a danger of breakage, and I know that the two sides maintained some sort of contact and there was some sort of reconnaissance, joint reconnaissance mission, but I don't have any details about what you're saying so I can neither -- I cannot either confirm nor deny it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I now have document P06405, one document before the one that you have in front of you now? The document number is P06405. Look under the caption, "East Mostar." Mortar fire was opened eight times in the course of the day. Further on, a reference is made to Budakovic who was the deputy commander of the 4th Corps of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It says a few days ago he stated that he wouldn't mind making a deal with the army of Bosnian Serbs in their common fight against Croats. Under 3 it says the civilian population is not happy with the way the humanitarian aid is distributed. The high officers of the BiH army are privileged in that respect. Under 3, under Jablanica, it says the chief of police speaks about the Mujahedin. Under item 3, the BiH army published that it had taken the Vitez and Vares pockets. Under item 5 which I'm interested in, and the rest was just information, early today a patrol confirmed that the -- a part of the Bijela bridge had been destroyed and that's the part that had not been destroyed prior to today. I repeat, today one patrol confirmed that a part of the Bijela bridge was destroyed and that's the part that had not been destroyed previously. Enclosed with this document is a drawing of the bridge before and after destruction. My question is this: Sir, the Bijela bridge, and we saw earlier who controlled the Bijela bridge, that was the BiH army, at your time, when you were there, was the BiH army in control of the Bijela Bridge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW
utterances.text: The ABiH had the control of the northern part of the Bijela Bridge, and I believe that the HVO controlled the southern access to the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Please, could you look at one of the images there? You'll see the whole Mostar valley. Please could you point the gentleman to the ELMO and show him the image? I've put it there for you. My question, while this is being done, is this: The bypass around the Bijela Bridge, a short bypass, before it was flooded by releasing the water from the dam in Salakovac, was it passable and before this destruction, was the Bijela Bridge also passable? Please look at the Mostar valley. I have put a circle around the Bijela Bridge, and I also marked the positions of the BiH army and the Republika Srpska army, and I also marked the positions of the HVO. Look that the circle and tell me whether it is at the point where the Bijela Bridge was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW
utterances.text: I think so but I say the same I said about the other map that I looked at.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, can you show me Vrdi on this map? As we sit here and as we speak, can you show the place where the positions of the HVO were at the time, and how was it possible for them to control the southern part of the Bijela Bridge? You passed that way. How do you think it was possible for them to control the southern part of the Bijela Bridge? Could you please show Vrdi on the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW
utterances.text: Once again, General, 14 years later, I cannot with any certainty remember the terrain, with any degree of certainty. I can say that a little towards Novo Potoci, and every time that we went towards Bijela we were shot at intensely by HVO troops. You may well ask why I say HVO troops. Well, because I saw them with my very own eyes from a house by the side of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm going to object to the question. It's not a game we're playing here. And if he wants to show the witness a map that has this place on it, then that's fine, but to simply show him a satellite image of a significant swath of western Herzegovina and ask him to pick out a position 14 years after the fact is unfair, and I object to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Praljak, the Prosecution is quite right. How can you expect this person to show you this place on the map, Vrdi, after 14 years?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am looking at a document, as simple as that. How can we know anything after 14 years? How can we know which house the fire came from and on what positions? I don't know how else I can ask this question. I can show documents to show where the fighting was taking place on the hill tops, how far was the main road from the HVO, and my principle question is this: Before the destruction that is mentioned here, when this happened, was prior to that the Bijela Bridge passable, and was there around it a bypass that was a macadam road which had been in use until the moment the water level rose and flooded the whole area? Would that be correct, would all this that I'm saying be correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW
utterances.text: You suggested and recommended that we use that bypass that went around towards Vijez [phoen] going up from the Bijela Bridge, if I'm not mistaken, the sapper unit in fact witness -- went to that area but we never used it. The idea was to try to repair the bridge, and as you well know, we came up with a solution eventually with a pontoon, but we never actually used that bypass that went around the Bijela Bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: I'm not saying anything about the pontoon bridge. All that is correct. But I'm asking you whether there was a bypass and before the destruction, could one use the Bijela Bridgeac at least to go over it in a little passenger vehicle? You were there. You know the situation. Could one use the bridge and the bypass before the destruction? I'm not claiming that you were the one who used the bridge or the bypass to go from one side to the other. I'm just asking you whether it was possible, using the bridge and the bypass.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW
utterances.text: I think not. As I said, the sapper unit went and for what we wanted to use the roads, to wit, to ferry the humanitarian convoys, we had to discard that route.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll stop for now because it's five minutes past 5.00. According to our calculations, Mr. Praljak's Defence counsel and himself have had 80 minutes, i.e. one hour and 20 minutes. We shall resume tomorrow morning at 9.00. Witness, you should of course, as you are under oath, not discuss this with anyone. You are a witness of the Chamber, and I would like you to come back tomorrow morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 4th day of October, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 5.06 p.m.,
